newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carrefour wants to up GMB stake-chairman.
newsitem.headline: Carrefour wants to up GMB stake-chairman.

text.p: French stores group Carrefour would like to raise its 40 percent stake in the GMB holding company which controls the Cora supermarket chain, Carrefour chairman Daniel Bernard said on Wednesday.

"We would like to go further of course," he told Reuters Financial Television. "We are already a big shareholder with more than 40 percent. But with that we cannot decide the strategy of the company," he said.
"This a good regional company, we think there are good synergies between Carrefour and this regional company, we could certainly develop the result and develop the company," he added.
"So we are hopeful we can go further but it is up to the majority shareholder to decide," he said.
Asked if he wanted to take control of Cora by the end of the year, he said "We cannot make any forecast on that."

Carrefour said on December 19 it had added an 8.1 percent stake to the 33.3 percent in Cora it bought the week before, bringing its total ownership in the privately-owned group to 41.4 percent. It paid a total 3.1 billion francs.
The group earlier posted 1996 net attributable pre-exceptional profit up 20.24 percent at 3.3 billion francs. Bernard said the results were in line with its forecasts.
The company will pursue international expansion, maintaining a rate of store openings in three new countries a year, he said.
"We continue our main strategy, to focus on global development, where we...have an advance of know-how, where we can rely on people of many countries to develop growth," he said.

Carrefour has stores in 17 compared to six countries five years ago, he said. "So we can develop a lot of new countries with a lot of potential like Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Mexico. We rely on this development to ensure our net profit in the future."
The group invested 13 billion francs last year, an increase of 72 percent, he said.
It plans to open stores this year in Poland -- its first eastern European country, Singapore and Indonesia.
Consumption was still weak in some countries, including France and Spain, while Mexico was slowly recovering. Brazil should improve but conditions in Argentina were still difficult, he said.
A recovery in French consumption would be highly selective and be demanding in terms of value for money and quality.

He declined to comment in detail on the recent sharp rise in Carrefour's share price but said, "I think in the global capitalisation of Carrefour, certainly there is (scope) to recognise the know-how of the group, to be a global partner because we can open (in) three countries a year...which is a very big risk and very challenging."
